keyVerseText: In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will:
rootMeaning: The Greek verb κληρόω (klēróō) derives from the noun κλῆρος (klēros), which fundamentally means a heritage, inheritance, or a lot assigned by chance. This root conveys the idea of receiving a portion or an acquisition, often as a result of casting lots or divine allotment. The literal sense of 'obtaining by lot' enriches the English gloss by emphasizing both the divine sovereignty and the element of appointed privilege or portion, rather than a mere possession.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, κληρόω appears with the specific meaning of obtaining an inheritance, as evidenced by its single recorded occurrence in Ephesians 1:11. The consistent translation as 'we have obtained an inheritance' highlights the certainty and divine appointment involved in the believer's portion. This usage underscores the theological theme of predestination and divine allotment, showing that the believer's inheritance is not random but purposefully assigned by God.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding κληρόω as 'to obtain an inheritance by divine allotment' deepens our grasp of God's sovereign work in salvation. It teaches that believers are not merely recipients of grace but are intentionally assigned a spiritual inheritance according to God's predestined plan. This verb affirms God's purposeful design in the distribution of blessings and privileges, emphasizing that our spiritual inheritance is secure and divinely ordained. It calls believers to recognize their place in God's eternal purpose and to live in the confidence of that inheritance through Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Ephesians 1:11 states, 'In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will.' Here, κληρόω highlights the believer's inheritance as a divinely appointed portion, secured in Christ. This word stresses that our spiritual blessings are not accidental but are granted by God's sovereign will and eternal counsel, providing profound assurance of our place in His redemptive plan.
